name: SiCamore Semi
old_description: More efficient drivetrains using semiconductor technologies based on Wide Band Gap (WBG) materials such as Silicon Carbide (SiC) are enabling engineers to achieve high voltage (1.2 – 3.3KV) and high power demands in a cost-effective way.
about:
SiCamore Semi operates a pure-play semiconductor foundry in Bend, Oregon. The company describes itself as a U.S.-based boutique foundry with three decades of experience in wafer fabrication, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly provided.

The foundry specializes in high-power, high-voltage wide-bandgap devices using silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) on 100 mm and 150 mm wafers. Its process flow covers photolithography with ASML 5000 I-line steppers and Karl Suss aligners, thin-film deposition (sputtering, PVD, CVD, PECVD, e-beam evaporation), frontside and backside metallization, thermal oxidation and diffusion, wet and dry etching (RIE), rapid thermal annealing, and ion implantation (cold and hot). SiC-specific steps include high-temperature implant and anneal, gate oxidation with nitric oxide anneal, and a dedicated gold wafer fab for high-reliability, radiation-hardened, and RF devices. Additional partner services encompass device design, wafer thinning, dicing, packaging, and test.

SiCamore serves electric-vehicle, medical, industrial, aerospace and defense, and academic customers. It supplies SiC diodes, MOSFETs, JBSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs, and Si SGTOs/SDIODEs for industrial power and switching applications. The company also collaborates with universities on NASA, NSF, DOE, and DOD grants focused on space, grid, weapons, EV, data-center, and communications technologies, and it targets U.S. military, intelligence, and government agencies alongside commercial transportation, telecommunications, and healthcare infrastructure markets.

The company states its mission is to deliver innovative power-semiconductor solutions through the development of silicon and wide-bandgap technologies. It aims to become the power-semiconductor facility in the U.S. Northwest for advanced wide-bandgap device fabrication, integration, and testing, emphasizing a stable, ITAR-certified environment for aerospace and defense programs.

name: Sierra Biomed - Autoclave and Medical Equipment Service and Repairs
old_description: Our Vision is To provide Peace of Mind for SPD managers, OR Managers and Biomed Departments by ensuring the highest reliability of equipment and being a one-call service provider for all SPD equipment
about:
Based in Aston Township, Pennsylvania, Sierra Biomed has spent more than four decades building a service organization focused on sterile processing equipment. The company operates across seven states from the Philadelphia–Washington corridor, deploying field service engineers who handle everything from routine inspections to emergency breakdowns.

Sierra Biomed does not manufacture equipment; instead it provides a single-source service model that covers preventative maintenance, emergency repair, installation, and the sale of both equipment and consumables. The firm maintains what it describes as the largest in-house inventory of preventative-maintenance and repair parts in the region, enabling a 93 percent first-time fix rate and a guaranteed 24-hour on-site response for emergencies. In 2025 its technicians logged more than 270,000 service miles across 485-plus customer sites.

The customer base includes hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, pharmaceutical firms, and laboratories. One named reference is SurgCenter of Towson, which relies on Sierra Biomed for sterilization equipment uptime. The company also serves biomedical departments and sterile processing managers who need consolidated contracts across multiple original equipment manufacturers.

Sierra Biomed says its differentiation lies in a 'one-call' capability that eliminates the need for multiple vendor contracts, a customer portal that provides real-time access to service records and job sheets, and a commitment to transparent communication backed by a 'make it right' guarantee if service falls short.

name: Sierra Metals
old_description: At Sierra Metals Southwest LLC, we specialize in crafting exceptional architectural and ornamental metals in the Las Vegas area. With a passion for precision and design, we offer both standard and custom solutions to elevate commercial, residential, or artistic spaces. From intricate details to bold elements our expert team delivers high quality metal work tailored to your vision.
about:
Sierra Metals Southwest LLC operates from a facility in Las Vegas, Nevada. The company does not publish a founding date, but its ownership group brings more than 40 years of metal‑fabrication experience to the business. Sierra Metals is part of a family of companies that includes Andy Russo Jr Inc, a union installation specialist, and Magnus Ornamental Metals, which focuses on ornamental and residential metalwork.

The shop provides architectural and ornamental metal fabrication using a range of processes: MIG welding of steel, TIG welding of stainless steel, brass and aluminum; shearing up to 3/16‑inch mild steel in 12‑foot lengths; ACM routing; polishing to #4, #6 and #8 finishes; light‑gauge bending up to 16 gauge in 12‑foot lengths; CAD design support; water‑jet cutting; and plasma cutting. From these capabilities it produces both standard and custom items such as fences, gates, decorative handrails and ceilings, door frames and guards, shade panels, louvers, trellises, security screens, art sculptures, ACM panels, metal soffit, fascia, trim, wall panels and standing‑seam roofing panels.

Sierra Metals serves commercial, residential and artistic clients in the Las Vegas region. Its customer base includes architects, general contractors, homeowners and artists. A noted collaboration is with F&A Modular Homes, for which Sierra Metals designs and fabricates metal components for modular housing units. The sister firms extend the offering to union‑grade installation and residential ornamental work.

The company states that its differentiation rests on four values: craftsmanship that blends skill with artistry, innovation that pushes custom solutions, customer focus that builds lasting relationships, and reliability that honors promises with timely service. This philosophy, coupled with the ownership’s deep industry tenure, is presented as the reason clients choose Sierra Metals for metalwork that is both functional and expressive.

about:
Sigla Furniture operates from a workshop and warehouse in Los Angeles, California. The business traces its roots to 1976 when the founder arrived from Iran; by the early 1980s he had opened a small woodworking shop after initially importing Italian music boxes. Now a second-generation, family-owned company, it has served the Los Angeles area for over four decades.

The company handcrafts traditional and transitional furniture — dining tables, sofas, chairs, case goods and accessories — each built to order in its Los Angeles facility using premium imported materials. Production relies on artisan joinery such as dovetail joints, custom wood finishing, and tailored upholstery in fabric, leather or velvet. Orders are made to specification from a sketch or SKU, with a typical lead time of eight to ten weeks.

Sigla serves residential clients, interior designers, and the hospitality sector. Commercial references include the Omni Hotel, the Shade Hotel and the Marriott. The 2022 acquisition of JDM Furniture and Unfinished Chairs added raw frame offerings and expanded capacity for large-scale projects.

The firm emphasizes heirloom-quality craftsmanship backed by a one-year repair guarantee (the Sigla Guarantee). Its family legacy and made-in-USA approach are positioned as the reason customers return for pieces intended to last generations.

old_description: The Lacing Tape Dispenser is made with the ease of use in mind. It helps keep your workbench organized, without having loose rolls of lacing tape rolling around in the workspace. Made of sturdy materials for use in the aerospace industry work environments. It feeds lacing tape to the technician with a weighted base to help prevent wasted material during the installation process.
about:
Silver State Wire & Cable Inc. began in 1991 in Sparks, Nevada, as a woman‑owned small business. It started as a modest value‑added service provider with two employees and three 1950s‑era wire processing machines, cutting and kitting wire, cable, and tubing for local assembly houses and OEMs.

Today the company provides wire processing, cable assembly, wiring harness fabrication, crimping, and electronic component testing, along with supply‑chain services such as kitting and just‑in‑time delivery. It also manufactures proprietary products including the Lacing Tape Dispenser, BRAIDLITE™ lightweight braided shielding for space applications, and the SumiMark IV Plus thermal‑transfer marking system. The operation serves programs ranging from hobby aircraft to satellites and fighter jets.

Silver State’s customer base spans aerospace, space, defense, and general aviation. Clients include OEMs building satellites, prime contractors rewiring fighter jets, and smaller shops assembling experimental aircraft. The company emphasizes on‑time delivery of exactly what each application requires, whether a single prototype or production quantities.

The firm cites its AS9100 and ISO 9001 certifications, ITAR registration, and WOSB status as foundations of its quality system. Management states that supporting customers remains the core of the business, with continuous improvement aimed at better service and reliable delivery for every order.

about:
Simplex Fabrication operates from Woodbine, Maryland, where owner Seth Neilson began the business roughly a decade ago. Neilson purchased an inexpensive TIG welder online and taught himself to weld on a personal vehicle in his garage, turning a hobby into a full-time fabrication shop.

The shop provides welding, metal fabrication, and CNC plasma cutting services. Work ranges from rust repair on automotive and equipment components to one-off custom builds such as a go-kart belt sander and a climbing saddle hunting tree stand. Neilson handles all production himself, offering quotes via call, text, or email.

Customers include individual hobbyists, equipment owners needing repairs, and anyone with a concept requiring metal fabrication. Projects have spanned automotive restoration, recreational vehicle modifications, and custom outdoor gear, though the company does not list specific industry verticals.

Neilson emphasizes continuous improvement, stating he enjoys "innovating better ways of doing things." The business grew from personal passion rather than a formal business plan, with a focus on bringing customer ideas to life regardless of scale.

about:
SinnovaTek was founded in 2015 in Raleigh, North Carolina, as a certified B Corporation with a mission to promote global health and wellness through sustainable food processing. The company was built on principles of integrity, creativity, and sustainability, aiming to deliver high-quality, healthy foods via advanced technologies.

The firm develops and manufactures advanced food processing equipment, including thermal processing systems and pumps, while providing R&D and engineering services. It operates a precision-scale aseptic copacking facility (FirstWave Co-Packing) for rapid prototyping and product launches, and offers protein-polyphenol ingredient technology (Vitero) with supporting product development and piloting services. The pilot facility enables small-scale manufacturing to commercialize products without traditional roadblocks.

SinnovaTek serves the food industry, working with both established companies and startups seeking to bring innovative food products to market. Its end-to-end solutions span equipment integration, ingredient technology, and co-manufacturing, targeting forward-thinking food businesses of all sizes.

The company differentiates itself through its B Corp certification, membership in the Upcycled Food Association, and a belief that processed foods can be nutritious and sustainable. It emphasizes making advanced technologies accessible to large and small companies alike, with creative, economical solutions that preserve nutrition and quality.

name: Siri Wire Co
old_description: who need mill-direct quality, real product knowledge, and a team that stands behind every order. We are
about:
Siri Wire Co. has operated from Danielson, Connecticut since its founding in 1992. The company is a fourth‑generation family business with more than 50 years of industry experience, and it remains led by the family that built it from the ground up.

The company manufactures and stocks stainless steel and alloy wire, serving customers across North America. Its product range includes electro‑polish quality (EPQ) wire — held in one of the largest domestic stocking positions in the region — as well as cold‑heading and spring wire grades such as 302, 304, 316, 17‑7, 302HQ, 303, 316L, 410, 416, 420, and 430. Siri Wire also provides annealing via strand annealing furnaces, coating and redraw services for customer‑supplied material, and straight‑and‑cut processing. Through its affiliation with Tri Star Metals and the Bender Wire Group, the company now operates behind two fully operational American production mills, enabling domestic melt, DFARS‑compliant, and non‑DFARS material options.

Siri Wire serves medical and surgical device manufacturers, aerospace and defense contractors, automotive suppliers, fastener and cold‑heading producers, filter screen and washer makers, and general industrial customers. Common applications include springs, fasteners, medical equipment, filter screens, washers, and rings.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001 certification, American‑made production, and a team that stands behind every order. Differentiators cited by the company include same‑day and short lead‑time shipping on stocked EPQ wire, the backing of two domestic mills for broader product range and engineering support, and a family‑owned culture focused on integrity and competitive pricing.

about:
Six B Apparel operates from Henderson, Nevada, producing custom dye-sublimated crew apparel for the racing industry. The company does not disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or the names of its founders in its public materials.

The shop specializes in all-over dye sublimation on lightweight, breathable polyester, delivering full-color, high-resolution prints that cover garments from neck to waist and sleeve to sleeve. Its process uses specially formulated dyes and a heat-transfer application that permanently bonds the image to the fabric, preventing peeling or fading through repeated washing. Products include custom crew shirts and hoodies, with an in-house art department handling design work for every order.

The primary customer base is race teams, from small grassroots outfits to larger operations, all seeking a professional, unified look. The company emphasizes that its no-minimum policy allows teams of any size to access the same quality of custom gear.

Six B Apparel positions its differentiators around three pillars: no minimum order quantities, an award-winning internal design team, and a combination of product quality, pricing, and customer service that it describes as rare in the market.
